container: Nanotechnology offers benefits across medicine, energy, agriculture, and manufacturing. Tiny materials can deliver drugs directly to diseased cells, improve imaging, and support diagnosis. Lightweight, durable composites can make vehicles more efficient, while coatings may resist corrosion and reduce cleaning needs. Nanostructured filters can remove pollutants, and improved batteries may store energy more effectively. However, these materials create risks. Their size may allow particles to enter lungs, tissues, or ecosystems, where long term effects remain uncertain. Production and disposal may expose workers and communities. Testing, transparent regulation, and design can help maximize benefits while limiting harm.
